chunks: Abu al-Hasan ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to Muḥammad ibn Sinān in what he wrote as a response to his questions:

The reason for wudu (ablution), for the sake of which it became incumbent upon the servant to wash the face and the forearms, and to wipe the head and the feet, is his standing before Allah, the Exalted, and his facing Him with his outward limbs, and his encountering thereby the noble recording angels.

So he washes the face for sajdah and humility; and he washes the hands so that he may turn them, seek with them, fear, and devote himself wholly; and he wipes the head and the feet because they are outward and uncovered, with which he faces all his states, and in them there is not the same degree of humility and devotion as there is in the face and the forearms.

key_terms.التَّبَتُّلِ: wholehearted devotion and detachment for worship
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before worship
key_terms.عِلَّةَ: the cause or reason underlying a ruling
key_terms.غَسْلُ: washing, as required for certain limbs in wudu
key_terms.مَسْحُ: wiping, as required for the head and feet in wudu

ai.seo_question: What is the reason for washing some limbs and wiping others in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the reason for wudu (ablution) in relation to standing before Allah, the Exalted, in worship. It describes how each act in wudu corresponds to outward humility, devotion, and readiness for salat (prayer), especially through the visible limbs that meet the noble recording angels.
